content.title: About
content.content: Huevos Rancheros is a classic Mexican dish consisting of fried eggs served on tortillas topped with a tomato‑chili sauce, beans, avocado, and cheese. It originated in the mid‑20th century and quickly became a popular hearty breakfast or brunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is often finished with a squeeze of fresh lime for bright acidity.
Tortillas can be corn or flour, depending on regional preference.
Traditional sauce is made from fresh tomatoes, chilies, onion, and cilantro.
Huevos Rancheros is commonly served with fried potatoes or black beans on the side.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Avocado and olive oil in the sauce supply monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and tomatoes deliver B6, B12, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and chilies are rich in lycopene and vitamin C, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Black beans and tortillas add dietary fiber, aiding normal digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs and should avoid the dish.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sauces and cheese can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of oil, avocado, and cheese makes the dish calorie‑rich; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Spicy ingredients
items.content: Chili peppers may irritate the stomach of those with sensitive digestive systems.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Huevos Rancheros hot: place tortillas on a plate, layer beans, sauce, fried eggs, sliced avocado, cheese, and fresh cilantro. Finish with lime juice and accompany with salsa or guacamole.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover tortillas in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Keep sauce and beans refrigerated in sealed containers for up to 3 days. Use fresh eggs and vegetables promptly.
